newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian minister raises tax reform poll.
newsitem.headline: Australian minister raises tax reform poll.

text.p: A senior Australian government minister on Sunday raised the possibility of holding a national referendum on the introduction of a goods and services tax (GST).
Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith said the proposal would reduce the political risk of introducing a GST and had found support within the ruling Liberal/National coalition.

"It politically has the benefit of clearing the decks before an election and getting a focussed discussion on (tax reform) rather than putting the government's political fortunes in jeopardy at a general election," Reith told Channel Seven's "Face to Face" programme.
Other options to advance tax reform included making the GST an election issue or calling an inquiry into tax reform which would report after the next federal election, Reith said.
Business, welfare and community groups are pressing the Australian government to reform the tax system, saying the present system is outdated.
The government is widely expected to propose some sort of consumption tax or GST in the next election campaign scheduled for early 1999.
Prime Minister John Howard has ruled out a GST during the government's current term, but recently revived the issue, saying tax reform was needed to create jobs.
The coalition's previous support for a GST was widely blamed for its loss in the 1993 election, when the then-ruling Labor party campaiged strongly against the tax.
Opposition Leader Kim Beazley last week said Labor would again not support a GST, but Reith said Labor was opposing the tax solely for political purposes.
